A maximum matching covers four nodes with two edges, and one more edge is needed for the fifth, so the minimum edge cover has three edges: A–B, B–C, and D–E, in the accent color; C–D is faded. Every node touches a chosen edge. The card lists the three edges and the count 5 − 2 = 3." width="100%"} An edge cover is a set of edges such that every node is an endpoint of at least one of them. The smallest one is built from a maximum matching, which covers two new nodes per edge, plus one extra edge for each node the matching leaves out. Edge covers model problems such as placing the fewest two-person patrols so that every post is visited, or picking the fewest links that still involve every station. A node without any incident edge cannot be covered, so the graph must have no isolated nodes. Edge direction is ignored. A self-loop can cover its node (when no other edge is available), but is never part of the matching. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The edge IDs of a minimum edge cover, in ascending order. An empty graph gives an empty list. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph has an isolated node. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Gallai's identity says that a minimum edge cover has $V - \nu$ edges, where $\nu$ is the size of a maximum matching. The method computes a maximum matching with Edmonds' blossom algorithm in $O(V^3)$ time and then, for each unmatched node, adds its incident edge with the lowest ID, as NetworkX does with an arbitrary incident edge. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a path of five nodes, a maximum matching covers four of them with two edges, and one more edge is needed for the last node: ::: {#1537b7a8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) path.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) cover = path.min_edge_cover() len(cover), path.is_edge_cover(cover) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (3, True) ``` ::: ::: A star needs every edge, since each leaf is only touched by its own edge: ::: {#259441a0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} star = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5) len(star.min_edge_cover()) == star.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
